newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt rallies at close on U.S. strength, euro.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt rallies at close on U.S. strength, euro.

* NZ two-year bonds pull yields lower at close
* Volumes reasonable
* Eurokiwi, dual currency issues boost bonds
New Zealand debt markets ended the week in style on Friday, with the two-year bond rallying 14 basis points and pulling other yields lower.

Dealers said a number of factors had combined to add to the market's strength, including a strong performance from U.S. Treasuries, and an overnight eurokiwi and samurai. Ontario joined the recent string of eurokiwi issuers in the two-year maturities with a NZ$100 million bond, and dealers said there were rumours of a seven billion yen dual currency issue.
The 90-day bank bills shed 17 basis points after Thursday's strong selling, to end back at 8.95 percent as the currency's Trade-Weighted Index climbed to 67.70 from its 67.41 close on Thursday.
Dealers said despite the volatility of the last couple of sessions, the 90-days were stuck in a fairly tight range of 8.75 to 9.25 percent.
December bank bill futures enjoyed a strong 10-point rally on the day to 91.48, and the rally in the 7/98 bond helped drag yields in the longer futures lower as well.
One bill dealer said the market had priced in an easing in the futures.

"It's probably not unreasonable -- I think the direction of the market is definitely downwards -- it's just a case of when do we get our next lot of economic information. It won't be for a couple of weeks, and until then it just continues to range-trade on the back of the currency," he said.
Cash bumped up to 9.50 percent from 9.45 percent on the back of around NZ$60 million worth of discounting, the dealer said.
Mid to long bonds shed five to seven points at the close, buoyed by the continued strength of the 7/98s and a bullish U.S. Treasury market.

U.S. jobless benefit claims on Thursday suggested a small slowdown in the labour market, boosting market sentiment ahead of crucial jobs data due at 1330 GMT. A Reuter poll shows analysts expecting non-farm payrolls to rise by 212,000 in October against a 40,000 drop in September. A figure around 200,000 is seen as a buying incentive.
It is also hoped the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index, due at 1500 GMT, will be market-friendly, with the potential to drive New Zealand bond yields lower at Monday's open.
